_comment: Curated modulator side of the metabolic-modulation readout: one rule per (perpetrator, enzyme), joined at read time against the `metabolism` table's substrate side. The database already knows which enzyme clears which substance; it does not know which substances inhibit or induce an enzyme, and that is the only thing stated here. One row therefore fans out to every substance that enzyme clears — 152 for CYP3A4 — which is why this is not a pair table like drug_interactions_pk.
_strength: Qualitative only — weak | moderate | strong. A fold-change is never stored: the readout says which way exposure moves and roughly how hard, and no figure ships that would read as measured.

_origin.substance: A logged co-active drug. Fires in the interaction checker when both it and a substrate are selected.
_origin.context: A lifestyle flag that is never logged as a dose (grapefruit, tobacco smoke), so it carries no matchers and surfaces only as substance-page education.
_origin.self: A drug modulating the enzyme that clears itself, so repeated doses build up disproportionately.

_matchers: Lowercased names that identify the perpetrator in a logged dose. Their own relation, kept out of `aliases`: three of these perpetrators (grapefruit, ritonavir, rifampicin, St John's Wort) have no substances row at all, and armodafinil's names are alias rows on Modafinil — keying on substance_id would merge two rules that carry different copy. See the pharmacology_matchers schema comment.
_uncited: Eight of the ten rules are qualitative textbook classifications carried over from the app's original hardcoded catalog and still carry no per-value citation. Two were checked in 2026-08 because they were suspected wrong, and both turned out to be right — see the `notes` on st-johns-wort and ritonavir, which also record what must not be changed back. The remaining eight (grapefruit, smoking, fluvoxamine, carbamazepine, rifampicin, modafinil, armodafinil, mdma-cyp2d6) are uncontroversial in direction but ungraded against a source; ground each against the FDA substrate/inhibitor/inducer table or the drug's own label before restating it as measured.

modulators.notes: CYP3A4 only, deliberately. Do not add a CYP2D6 arm: the case for one is Henry & Hill's single fatality on ritonavir plus MDMA (pmid:9848354), and de la Torre's reply in the same journal (pmid:10029010, read in full) names three confounders — alcoholic liver impairment, ritonavir started two weeks earlier, CYP2D6 status never determined — and offers MDMA's own non-linear kinetics as the alternative: across a 3-fold dose range (50-150 mg) its AUC rose 10-fold. Piru already models that saturation, so attributing it to ritonavir would double-count one mechanism. The reply also states ritonavir's CYP2D6 interactions are 'less relevant than those associated with CYP3A'.

Moderate is right, and was checked because it was suspected of understating a strong inducer. Wang 2001's probe-cocktail study in 12 healthy subjects found long-term St John's wort cut ORAL midazolam AUC by >50% while cutting IV midazolam AUC only 20% — induction of intestinal CYP3A, largely not hepatic. A >50% oral AUC fall sits in the moderate band, not the >=80% strong one. The same study found no change in CYP1A2, CYP2C9 or CYP2D6 activity, so the single-enzyme rule is right too. Confidence stays medium because hyperforin content varies several-fold between preparations and the induction tracks it.
